answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by pricing identity through bonded reputation. Each agent locks a stake and gains influence only from independently verified, completed tasks, so reputation builds like an ember and is slashed at once for fraud. Influence grows with the square root of stake, so splitting into many copies, each as hard as onyx, adds no power. Even a rising tide of fake accounts must pay a bond, do real work, and risk forfeiture for each one, making mass forgery unprofitable.
